hitl_conditions: Planners accept/reject every recommendation; human judgement covers internal business rules and expertise absent from the data; each response feeds the RL reward so the model improves over time. No future reduction of the human role is stated.
key_finding: A distributed logistics DT (Azure Digital Twins + Databricks) streams fleet telematics and ERP orders into an RL job-assignment/routing model; planners accept or reject its recommendations and their responses act as RL reward. Preliminary what-if simulations on 2023 company data indicate a 20-30% carbon-footprint reduction from avoided empty runs.

quotes.text: Using the Digital Twin Definition Language (DTDL) [28], we created a JSON-based model depicting the virtual representation of our operations, syncing in real time with our data lakehouse.
The case study is simply that of the pick-up and drop-off segment of the transport company in which assets are transported based on customer orders across the UK.
The recommendation system is based on a reinforcement learning with human feedback model and a traveling salesman problem algorithm for route optimization.
The RL model formulated as an MDP is trained with the environment, specifying the state, action, transition and reward, as described in Section 2 of this paper.
The system recommends optimized plans to transport planners, who accept or reject the proposal, from which the RL model uses as a reward (human feedback) to improve.

The use of a human-in-the-loop approach enables the model to learn from other factors such as internal business rules that require human intelligence, which the data and trends about jobs and driver proximity do not take into account.
